story: Until 2026-12-29 (32 days), options price BHEL to move about ±7.5%, roughly 392 to 455. In the past, the price ended inside the range priced this way 57% of the time.

Calls and puts the same distance from the price cost about the same (gap +0.9 vol points): no strong demand for either protection or upside. Puts usually cost more than this for BHEL: against the past year the gap is on the high side, so less fear is priced than usual.
BHEL futures trade 1.5 points above the price itself. That premium works out to 4.0% a year, within its usual range for the past year.
BHEL has actually been moving about 2.22% a day this past month: normal for it against the past year.

iv.simple: Options on BHEL are priced for moves of about 2.02% a day. That is normal for BHEL compared with the past year.
iv.analyst: 30-day constant-maturity ATM IV 32.0%: 35th percentile of 1 year, 10th of all days since 2019-01-01.

vrp.simple: Options are cheap compared with how much BHEL has actually been moving: they price 32.0% a year while the last month realised 35.2%.
vrp.analyst: IV30 - RV21 = -3.1 vol points, 48th percentile of the past year. Since 2019-01-01, IV30 was above the volatility that actually followed over the next 21 sessions on 64% of days: option sellers are usually paid a premium for carrying the risk, and the gap is what that premium looks like today.

skew.simple: Calls and puts the same distance from the price cost about the same (gap +0.9 vol points): no strong demand for either protection or upside. Puts usually cost more than this for BHEL: against the past year the gap is on the high side, so less fear is priced than usual.
skew.analyst: 25-delta risk reversal +0.89 vol pts (front month), 82nd percentile of the past year. More negative = more demand for downside insurance relative to upside.

realised.simple: BHEL has actually been moving about 2.22% a day this past month: normal for it against the past year.
realised.analyst: RV21 35.2% (31st percentile of the past year), RV5 34.2%, RV63 39.1%; RV5/RV63 compression at the 42nd percentile.

oi.simple: For the 2026-12-29 expiry, the biggest pile of call positions is at 430 (+1.9% away) and the biggest pile of put positions is at 400 (-5.2%). Option sellers defend these levels, so price often slows near them, but they shift as positions change.
oi.analyst: Front-expiry PCR (OI) 0.63; all-expiry OI PCR at the 39th percentile of the past year. Today's change: calls +1,443,750, puts +215,250 (OI units, i.e. shares or index quantity). A high PCR in India mostly reflects put writing, so it is read as crowding, not as a signal.

futures.simple: BHEL futures trade 1.5 points above the price itself. That premium works out to 4.0% a year, within its usual range for the past year.
futures.analyst: Near-month basis +1.5, annualised carry 4.0% (18th percentile of the past year; its 1-year median 6.6%). Last 5 sessions (price x OI, same contracts day to day): Short build-up, Short build-up, Short build-up, Short covering, Short covering. Build-up labels describe what happened to positions; they do not say who is right.

move.simple: Until 2026-12-29 (32 days), options price BHEL to move about ±7.5%, roughly 392 to 455. In the past, the price ended inside the range priced this way 57% of the time.
move.analyst: ATM straddle / forward = 7.51% (forward 423.5). Scored on 1,826 days since 2019-01-01 against the official close on each expiry; a straddle is the market's mean absolute move, so about 57% inside is what a fair price would give.

notes.text: BHEL has used 39% of its market-wide position limit (the ban starts at 95%).
Lot size changes from 2,625 to 1,250 for the 2027-01-25 contracts (the exchange has already listed them so).
